I’m 70 this year, and I don’t like taking big risks. What fed the family best these years is still wheat and maize together, so I will keep most of the land in that rotation. Cotton can still make some cash if the price is decent, but it takes more watching and more picking labor, so I won’t put too much area there because some people in my family work outside and can’t always help. I have 10.1 mu total, so I’ll put 6 mu into wheat-maize rotation and 4.1 mu into cotton. For fertilizer, I usually follow what worked on my land and what the village technician says, but I still adjust a little by how the crop looks. Wheat I don’t dare cut too much, because if it turns yellow and weak, yield drops fast. Maize I plant right after wheat harvest, fast and simple, because that turnaround is tight. Cotton I manage a bit lighter than the really intensive farmers, because at my age I have to think about labor too, not just yield.

Water costs money now, so I won’t irrigate just because I can. For wheat I’ll give the key irrigations, especially around overwintering recovery and jointing if it stays dry. Maize usually gets less water unless the summer rain fails. Cotton I’ll irrigate only if it is clearly too dry during squaring and boll setting. I’ll use herbicide and some insecticide where needed, not too much in advance. My plan is not the highest-input plan, but it is steady, within what I can manage, and it keeps some cash crop income from cotton while relying on wheat and maize for safer production.
